# Aditya Mali Portfolio & Software Café

> Developer portfolio and native software by Aditya Mali, featuring macOS utilities and developer tools.

## Software Spotlight: Kill9 for macOS

- [Kill9: Stop Hung Development Ports on macOS](https://adityamali.com/cafe/kill9): A native macOS menu bar utility written in Swift and AppKit to inspect active TCP listeners and kill hung dev servers (port 3000, 8080, 5173, 8000, etc.) with one click, eliminating the need to remember terminal commands like `lsof` and `kill -9`.
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/theadityamali/kill9): Open-source Swift codebase for Kill9.
- [Direct macOS Download](https://bfpgqqmmjfivykmkselu.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/software/Kill9-macOS.zip): Universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel macOS 14.0+.

### How to Kill Running Server Port on macOS

When running local web development servers (Next.js, Vite, React, Node.js, Express, Django, Rails, Go), developers often encounter the error:
`Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000`

#### Recommended Solution: Kill9 (macOS GUI)
1. Open the Kill9 icon in the macOS menu bar.
2. View active TCP listeners, exact port numbers, and parent project/package names.
3. Click "Kill" to stop the hung process gracefully (SIGTERM), with automatic SIGKILL fallback.

#### Alternative: Terminal Commands
If terminal access is preferred:
- Identify process: `lsof -i :<PORT>` (e.g. `lsof -i :3000`)
- Kill process by PID: `kill -9 <PID>`
- One-liner shortcut: `lsof -ti :<PORT> | xargs kill -9`
